explain.say: In 27 BCE Octavian stood before the Roman Senate and announced he was handing the Republic back to the Senate and people. They gave him a new name, Augustus, and he ruled alone for forty years. How did a republic that hated kings end up with an emperor? Look at the board: five causes.

explain.say: Start with land. Rich Romans built huge estates worked by enslaved people, while many small farmers lost their land. In 133 BCE the tribune Tiberius Gracchus pushed a land reform, and senators beat him to death. See it on the timeline. Why might killing a reformer change politics for everyone afterwards?

explain.say: Now the second cause, private armies. From about 107 BCE Marius recruited poor volunteers, who expected land from their general after service. So soldiers trusted generals more than the Senate. In 88 BCE Sulla marched his army on Rome itself. Can you guess what Caesar did in 49 BCE?

explain.say: Look at the map. Caesar conquered Gaul, today's France, and grew rich and popular. In 49 BCE he crossed the Rubicon river with his army, starting a civil war. Made dictator for life, he was assassinated on the Ides of March, 44 BCE. His heir Octavian defeated Antony and Cleopatra at Actium, in Greece, in 31 BCE, and took Egypt.

Augustus kept the Senate, the consuls and the old names, but held the armies. In 1939 Ronald Syme's The Roman Revolution called him a party boss who seized power. Others stress the peace he brought after a century of civil war. Great job. Exam tip: link each cause to a named event and a date.

faq.a: After defeating Antony and Cleopatra at Actium in 31 BCE, Octavian controlled the armies. In 27 BCE he claimed to restore the Republic and received the name Augustus, keeping republican offices while holding real power as princeps, first citizen.
asks: Who was the first Roman emperor?
What did Augustus claim in 27 BCE?

faq.a: The brothers Tiberius and Gaius Gracchus, tribunes who proposed land reform and help for poorer citizens. Tiberius was killed in 133 BCE and Gaius in 121 BCE, opening an age of political violence.

faq.q: Why were Roman armies loyal to their generals?
faq.a: From around 107 BCE, generals like Marius recruited poor volunteers who depended on their commander for pay and land after service. Soldiers' loyalty shifted from the state to the man who led and rewarded them.

faq.q: What does crossing the Rubicon mean?
faq.a: In January 49 BCE Julius Caesar led his army across the Rubicon, the border of Italy, which it was illegal for a general to cross under arms. It began civil war, and the phrase now means a point of no return.
asks: Why did Caesar cross the Rubicon?

faq.a: Senators led by Brutus and Cassius feared his power after he was made dictator for life in 44 BCE. They killed him on 15 March 44 BCE, hoping to save the Republic, but civil war followed.

facts: Tiberius Gracchus was killed in 133 BCE.
Julius Caesar was assassinated on 15 March 44 BCE.
Octavian received the name Augustus in 27 BCE.
